title: evaluation / Score an existing dataset
content: ## Score an existing dataset Standalone scoring evaluates recorded outputs without rerunning the model or agent that produced them. Use it to assess an exported application dataset, or to try an evaluator against known responses before adding it to an agent test suite. 1. In **Foundry Toolkit**, select **Developer Tools** > **Monitor** > **Evaluation**. 2. On **Overview**, select **Add Evaluation**. 3. Enter an evaluation name, select evaluators, and select a judge model if required. 4. Import a dataset with the required columns, or choose the sample dataset to explore the workflow. 5. Open the created evaluation, review the input data, and select **Run Evaluation**. 6. Review the job status, logs, and result table. Check failed or incomplete rows before interpreting aggregate scores. ![Screenshot showing the standalone Evaluation overview with Overview and Evaluators tabs, an existing job, and the Add Evaluation action.](./images/evaluation/evaluation-overview.png) The job's configuration, logs, and results are stored locally under the user's `.aitk` directory. These standalone jobs are not automatically published to Foundry or saved in the open workspace. For further analysis, select **Open in Data Wrangler** in the standalone result view. This action uses the [Data Wrangler extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-toolsai.datawrangler). It differs from the **Data Viewer** used for pytest and downloaded Foundry results below. ### Create a custom evaluator Use a custom evaluator when the built-in metrics do not cover a requirement such as a response format or a domain-specific quality criterion. 1. In the standalone **Evaluation** view, select **Evaluators** > **Create Evaluator**. 2. Enter a **Name** and **Description**. 3. Select **LLM-based** or **Code-based (Python)**. 4. Define the criterion or code, then select **Save**. 5. Select the saved evaluator when creating an evaluation job. For an LLM-based evaluator, define a scoring scale, examples, and the expected JSON output. Use variables such as {{query}} and {{response}}. The **Prompt example** selector provides starting points. For example, request a result with a score and explanation: ```json {"score":4,"reason":"The response addresses the question but omits one required detail."} ``` For a code-based evaluator, edit the generated Python scaffold and preserve its method signature. Return a score and, when useful, a reason. If it requires external Python libraries, configure the Python environment and dependencies requested by the Toolkit. ![Screenshot showing the custom evaluator form with Name, Description, LLM-based and Code-based (Python) choices, and prompt configuration.](./images/evaluation/custom-evaluator-form.png)
